item.title: Topic Overview
item.description: Spiking Neural Networks Spiking neural networks are neural networks that compute with events in time.

item.title: 1. Why SNNs Need Events
item.description: 1. Why SNNs Need Events Build up why snns need events one step at a time.

item.title: 1.1 Why Spiking Neural Networks Exist
item.description: Why Spiking Neural Networks Exist Imagine a small camera watching a quiet hallway.

item.title: 1.2 Spikes, Timing, and Event-Driven Computation
item.description: Spikes, Timing, and Event-Driven Computation A temporal event stream already gives you a different kind of input from a fixed table of numbers: events arrive at particular moments, and long stretches may contain little activity.

item.title: 1.3 The Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neuron
item.description: The Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neuron Imagine the spike train from the previous idea arriving at one neuron as a sequence of tiny taps: one spike arrives now, another arrives a moment later, then silence, then a short burst.

item.title: 1.4 Excitation, Inhibition, and Winner-Take-All Competition
item.description: Excitation, Inhibition, and Winner-Take-All Competition A single spiking neuron can already do something useful: it can collect incoming spike events, let its membrane potential rise, and fire when the accumulated evidence crosses a threshold.

item.title: 2. Accuracy Formula, Correct Prediction Count, Total Prediction Count Formula Mechanics
2.1 Accuracy as Correct Decisions
item.description: After you already know what a prediction is, accuracy gives you a compact way to judge a model’s decisions across many prediction attempts.
